description: The shipped default-UI panel manifest: panel key -> the scene that serves it, plus the Insimul modules (band 111, conformance/modules/genre-activation.json) a panel needs before it is offered at all. This file is DATA on purpose — insimul_ui_registry.gd resolves through it and spells no panel key and no module id, so adding or gating a panel is a data change, not an engine change. tools/verify-ui/check-ui.mjs holds it to conformance/ui/registry-cases.json -> panel_keys and checks every scene and every module id. v3 adds the PAUSE-MENU TAB MAP: which shipped panel serves each ESC-menu tab, so the menu resolves its bodies through the registry and spells no panel key either.

panelTiers.pinned: No `pending_corpus` field: the key is in the shared corpus's panel_keys and the two lists must match EXACTLY, both ways. This is the cross-engine registry contract.
panelTiers.ahead_of_corpus: A `pending_corpus` field: a panel this port ships before the shared corpus documents the key. The field says what has to happen for it to become pinned (core adds the key, then `npm run vendor:conformance`), and the gate refuses a `pending_corpus` entry whose key the corpus ALREADY documents — so the tier is a waiting room, not a parking lot. Same accounting idiom as NOT_ADOPTED in check-mechanics.mjs.
panelTiers.gate_note: Required on an ahead-of-corpus panel that declares no `requires`: say which module WOULD back it and why none does. An ungated panel is an answer, not an omission.

hud.note: a COMPOSITE — it mounts its children through the registry, so each one still meets the module gate on the way in

game_menu.note: a COMPOSITE — the in-game menu SHELL. It mounts the tabbed pause menu and the notification centre through the registry, so each meets the module gate on the way in, and forwards open/close to whichever child is a menu.

skill_tree.pending_corpus: conformance/ui/registry-cases.json -> panel_keys does not document skill_tree yet; move this entry to the pinned tier when core adds the key and the corpus is re-vendored

minimap.pending_corpus: core has no minimap key yet; re-vendor and pin when it does

fullmap.pending_corpus: core has no fullmap key yet; re-vendor and pin when it does

quickbar.pending_corpus: core has no quickbar key yet; re-vendor and pin when it does

radial_menu.pending_corpus: core has no radial_menu key yet; re-vendor and pin when it does

notice_board.gate_note: no band-111 module backs a notice board: notices are core world content, and quests are not a module. Gating it on the nearest module (routine) would hide the board in the educational / language-learning bundles, which activate no modules at all and are exactly the worlds this repo's own templates post notices in. The narrative-placement module of tasklist 195 is the one that would back it.
notice_board.pending_corpus: core has no notice_board key yet; re-vendor and pin when it does

documents.gate_note: no band-111 module backs a reader: readable content is core world content. `equipment` is the nearest (a book is an item) and is the wrong answer — it would take the reader away from every genre bundle that activates nothing, which is where reading practice actually lives.
documents.pending_corpus: core has no documents key yet; re-vendor and pin when it does

pauseMenuTabs_doc: The ESC menu's tab bodies, as data. A tab key (InsimulPauseMenuModel.DEFAULT_TABS, mirrored from conformance/ui/pause-menu-cases.json) -> the panel key that serves it. insimul_ui_registry.gd answers it (tab_panel/tab_panels) and pause_menu.gd mounts the answer through instantiate(), so a tab body meets the band-111 module gate on the way in exactly like a HUD child does — and the two gates stack: the tab shows when the pause-menu MODULE BUNDLE enables it, and its body appears when the world activates the panel's module. `pauseMenuTabNotes` accounts for every tab no panel serves; check-ui.mjs holds the two together against the shipped tab set, totally and both ways, so a tab can never be silently empty. `pauseMenuCloseTab` is the one tab that dismisses the menu instead of showing a body.

pauseMenuTabNotes.resume: the close affordance, not a body — see pauseMenuCloseTab
pauseMenuTabNotes.character: no shipped panel: the character sheet is the `proficiency` module's own surface and the shared corpus documents no panel key for it. The host mounts its own body here until core adds one.
pauseMenuTabNotes.vocabulary: no shipped panel: vocabulary review is the language-learning bundle's surface (SRS state lives in currentState.languageProgress) and the shared corpus documents no panel key for it.
pauseMenuTabNotes.analytics: no shipped panel: conversation analytics render a report over save.conversations, and the shared corpus documents no panel key for it.
pauseMenuTabNotes.assessment: no shipped panel: assessments are the `assessment` module's own surface and the shared corpus documents no panel key for it.
pauseMenuTabNotes.settings: no shipped panel: engine settings (resolution, audio, input) are the GAME's, not Insimul's — a default-UI settings screen would be the addon dictating a project's options.
